feature_functions.description: The floor and walls plausibly form a mounting region for omitted wheel-support hardware.

feature_behaviors.name: Permit wheel motion
feature_behaviors.description: Clearance between the cavity walls and wheel allows rotational motion.

feature_behaviors.name: React mounting contact
feature_behaviors.description: The recess floor could react loads from an omitted support or axle carrier.

relationships.description: The pocket surrounds the local wheel region and provides operational clearance.
The pocket establishes the wheel position relative to the housing centerline.
The recess is cut into the central portion of the upper shell.

brep_faces.name: First longitudinal pocket wall
brep_faces.description: One planar side wall of the wheel-clearance pocket.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar quadrilateral face with area 229.601413 mm^2.
Its normal is predominantly along CAD X and its y-z bounding extent matches a recess side wall.
It pairs geometrically with FACE 2.

brep_faces.name: First transverse pocket wall
brep_faces.description: One planar end wall of the wheel-clearance pocket.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar quadrilateral face with area 95.738389 mm^2.
Its normal is predominantly along CAD Z.
Its bounding box adjoins the side-wall extents of FACE 0 and FACE 2.

brep_faces.name: Second longitudinal pocket wall
brep_faces.description: Planar side wall opposite FACE 0.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar quadrilateral face with area 229.499683 mm^2.
Its normal is predominantly along CAD X and opposite that of FACE 0.
Its dimensions closely match FACE 0, supporting interpretation as the opposite pocket wall.

brep_faces.name: Second transverse pocket wall
brep_faces.description: Planar end wall opposite FACE 1.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar quadrilateral face with area 59.211795 mm^2.
Its normal is predominantly along CAD Z and opposite that of FACE 1.
Its location near CAD z=59.22 mm closes the opposite end of the recess.

brep_faces.name: Pocket floor
brep_faces.description: Planar bottom surface of the wheel-clearance recess and a plausible seat for omitted support hardware.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar quadrilateral face at constant y=10.000000 mm.
Its normal is aligned with CAD Y.
Its x-z bounding box lies within the four planar pocket walls.
The geometry is consistent with the floor of a blind recess.

sections.name: Scroll wheel component
sections.description: Separate rounded wheel represented by SOLID 1. Its toroidal perimeter is intended for finger engagement, while its planar side faces provide potential axial locating interfaces.
sections.location: Centered over and partially within the wheel-clearance pocket, with its rotational axis approximately parallel to CAD Y.

section_functions.name: Receive finger input
section_functions.description: Provides an exposed rounded control surface for user engagement.

section_functions.name: Guide rotational input
section_functions.description: Converts tangential finger motion into rotation about the transverse wheel axis.

section_behaviors.name: Permit rotation
section_behaviors.description: The wheel is intended to rotate relative to the stationary housing.

section_behaviors.name: React finger contact
section_behaviors.description: The rounded perimeter reacts tangential and normal loads applied by a finger.

features.name: Scroll wheel
features.description: Compound rounded wheel feature comprising a toroidal finger-contact tread and two planar axial side faces.

feature_functions.name: Engage the user's finger
feature_functions.description: Acts as the movable control element of the mouse.

feature_functions.name: Guide scroll input
feature_functions.description: Supports controlled movement along a rotational path.

feature_behaviors.name: Rotate within the recess
feature_behaviors.description: The wheel geometry supports rotation about its approximate CAD-Y axis.

feature_behaviors.name: React user input
feature_behaviors.description: Carries normal and tangential finger contact loads.

relationships.description: The lower portion of the wheel occupies the housing's clearance pocket.
The compound scroll wheel contains the rounded tread feature.
The compound scroll wheel contains the axial side-interface feature.

features.name: Rounded finger-contact tread
features.description: The exposed rounded perimeter of the scroll wheel, realized by two adjoining toroidal faces.

feature_functions.name: Provide finger grip
feature_functions.description: Provides the contact surface through which the user rotates the wheel.

feature_functions.name: Engage finger motion
feature_functions.description: Receives tangential input from the user's finger.

feature_behaviors.name: React tangential contact
feature_behaviors.description: The toroidal surface reacts finger pressure and tangential force.

feature_behaviors.name: Move along a rotational path
feature_behaviors.description: The rounded tread passes through the housing opening as the wheel rotates.

relationships.description: The tread is a subfeature of the complete scroll wheel.
The rounded tread terminates at the two planar wheel side faces.
The tread is positioned along the longitudinal extent of the wheel-clearance pocket.

brep_faces.name: First tread half
brep_faces.description: One toroidal portion of the rounded wheel perimeter.
evidence: CadQuery reports a TORUS with major radius 4.282455 mm and minor radius 3.000000 mm.
Its bounding box spans y=15.069459 to 29.133459 mm around the wheel center.
Visual correspondence identifies this surface as part of the exposed green scroll-wheel tread.

brep_faces.name: Second tread half
brep_faces.description: The opposing toroidal portion completing the rounded wheel perimeter.
evidence: CadQuery reports a TORUS with major radius 4.032000 mm and minor radius 3.000000 mm.
It has the same y extent as FACE 11 and an adjacent x-z envelope.
Together FACE 11 and FACE 13 account for the rounded outer wheel surface visible in all relevant views.

features.name: Axial wheel side interfaces
features.description: Opposed planar side faces of the wheel. These faces can provide axial clearance or locating contact with omitted supports; the supplied model contains no explicit axle or bore.

feature_functions.name: Provide axial locating surfaces
feature_functions.description: The opposed planar sides can establish the wheel's transverse position if contacted by supports.

feature_functions.name: Provide side clearance
feature_functions.description: The planar sides define the wheel's axial envelope relative to the recess.

feature_behaviors.name: Allow axial constraint
feature_behaviors.description: Contact at the opposed planar faces could constrain translation along the wheel axis.

feature_behaviors.name: React axial contact
feature_behaviors.description: The side faces can react axial loads from omitted support members.

relationships.description: The side interfaces are subfeatures of the complete wheel.
The side-face envelope lies within the transverse bounds of the central recess.

brep_faces.name: First axial wheel face
brep_faces.description: Planar side face on one axial side of the scroll wheel.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar face with centroid (25.525387,22.101459,51.311858).
Its normal is predominantly along CAD X.
The face is bounded by one closed edge and lies directly beside toroidal FACE 11.

brep_faces.name: Second axial wheel face
brep_faces.description: Planar side face opposite FACE 12.
evidence: CadQuery reports a planar face with centroid (30.324044,22.101459,51.198346).
Its normal is predominantly along CAD X and opposite that of FACE 12.
The face is bounded by one closed edge and lies beside toroidal FACE 13.
